sections.heading: C2 — Impairment and penalty confusables
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Impairment and penalty confusables with knowledge-graph hints

FACT_ID: sec08-R01 | anchor: A35
Failing the chemical test costs forty five days plus six interlock months, while refusing every test costs forty five days plus a full interlock year. [A35]
Why it matters: group_hint fail-vs-refuse; prereq_hint sec08-F11; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec08-F11, sec08-F13.
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0035]
FACT_ID: sec08-R02 | anchor: A35
Drivers under twenty one face zero tolerance at two hundredths percent on public roads and private lots alike, with failures drawing forty five days and a year minimum interlock. [A35]
Why it matters: group_hint teen-tolerance; prereq_hint sec08-F12; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec08-F12, sec08-F13.
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0035]
FACT_ID: sec08-R03 | anchor: A35
A shot and a half of liquor, a regular beer, or a five ounce wine each count one drink, while fancy mixed drinks can secretly equal several. [A35]
Why it matters: group_hint drink-math; prereq_hint sec08-F06; difficulty_hint 1; confusable_with sec08-F05, sec08-F06.
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0035]
FACT_ID: sec08-R04 | anchor: A35
Coffee, fresh air, workouts and cold showers never speed sobriety; only elapsed time clears alcohol from the body. [A35]
Why it matters: group_hint sober-myths; prereq_hint sec08-F07; difficulty_hint 1; confusable_with sec08-F07.
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0035]
FACT_ID: sec08-R05 | anchor: A35
Cold, headache, allergy and nerve medicines alone mimic liquor behind the wheel, and stacked with liquor they multiply toward grave illness or death. [A35]
Why it matters: group_hint pill-stack; prereq_hint sec08-F09; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec08-F09, sec08-F10.
Source: [A35 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0035]
FACT_ID: sec08-R06 | anchor: A36
Teen phone tickets climb thirty, ninety, then one hundred eighty days, while teen twenty over speeding climbs sixty, ninety, then one hundred eighty days. [A36]
Why it matters: group_hint ladder-pairs; prereq_hint sec08-F16; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec08-F16, sec08-F17.
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0036]
FACT_ID: sec08-R07 | anchor: A36
First GDL and reckless counts add up to thirty jail days, but first street racing counts add up to a full jail year. [A36]
Why it matters: group_hint jail-split; prereq_hint sec08-F18; difficulty_hint 3; confusable_with sec08-F18, sec08-F19.
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0036]
FACT_ID: sec08-R08 | anchor: A36
Repeat restriction breaks span six months or stretch to the eighteenth birthday, whichever lasts longer, on top of the per offense ladders. [A36]
Why it matters: group_hint until-eighteen; prereq_hint sec08-F15; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec08-F14, sec08-F15.
Source: [A36 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0036]
FACT_ID: sec08-R09 | anchor: A37
Under eighteen, negligent homicide with a motor vehicle, evading a crash causing death or serious injury, and DUI of alcohol or drugs bar youthful offender status, whereas youthful offender adjudications for reckless driving, driving under suspension, evading a property-damage or non-serious-injury crash, street racing, or eluding police are disclosed to DMV for suspension [A37].
Why it matters: group_hint youth-split; prereq_hint sec08-F20; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec08-F20, sec08-F21.
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0037]
FACT_ID: sec08-R10 | anchor: A37
Drivers age twenty-four or younger with two or more moving or suspension violations, and drivers age twenty-five or older with three or more such convictions, must complete certified operator retraining, and another moving violation within three years of completion brings a suspension of at least thirty days [A37].
Why it matters: group_hint retrain-math; prereq_hint sec08-F24; difficulty_hint 2; confusable_with sec08-F24, sec08-F25, sec08-F26.
Source: [A37 -> src:rdmv-ct-d:connecticut-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0037]
